title: Nepal’s floods put the global loss and damage system to the test
gist: Nepal's August glacial flood (over 1,400 dead, $4-5bn damage, about a tenth of GDP) is a first stress test of the UN loss-and-damage fund, whose resources are tiny relative to need, and sets up attribution and responsibility fights at COP31.

insights.claim: The 26 August glacial flood in Nepal's Bhotekoshi and Rasuwa region killed over 1,400 people, and reconstruction is estimated at $4 to 5 billion, around a tenth of GDP, though Nepal emits only about 0.1% of global greenhouse gases.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Illustrates tail climate-loss risk for low-emitting, fiscally small states.

insights.claim: As of March 2026, 27 countries pledged $822.06 million to the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, only about half received; its first round offered $342 million against roughly $2.8 billion in requests.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Climate finance remains far below need; delivery risk is high.

insights.claim: The FRLD caps projects at $20 million, has no rapid-access pathway outside application windows and faces World Bank approval bottlenecks, so Nepal's $20 million request tests whether it can disburse quickly.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Credibility test for the fund ahead of COP31.

insights.claim: The ICJ's July 2025 advisory opinion accepted that climate science can link specific disasters to climate change and set a 'sufficiently direct and certain' causality standard, giving partial legal footing for claims.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Raises long-run liability risk for large emitters.

insights.claim: Nepal is pushing major emitters, including China and India which argue differentiated responsibility, to share costs, but translating this into binding finance obligations will be hard; the US withdrawal from UNFCCC complicates COP31.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Expect contested burden-sharing and weak near-term outcomes.

insights.claim: India relies on Nepalese hydropower and China and India invest in the region's infrastructure, giving both strategic interest in recovery; Nepal's PM proposed a Himalayan Climate Resilience Mechanism with India and China.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Regional cooperation on glacial-lake data and early warning may be the achievable outcome.

insights.claim: Chatham House says COP31 should prioritize clearer attribution standards for multi-causal disasters, consistent valuation of economic and non-economic losses, and faster, more predictable FRLD finance, with incremental rather than transformational progress likely amid fiscal strain.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Set expectations low for COP31 loss-and-damage outcomes.
